newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish ex-premier denies state terrorism existed.
newsitem.headline: Spanish ex-premier denies state terrorism existed.

text.p: Spain's former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, whose 13-year government is being investigated on allegations it ran a "dirty war" against Basque separatists, said on Thursday his country was not guilty of state terrorism.

"Clearly, there hadn't been state terrorism in Spain," Gonzalez told a Spanish radio interviewer. "If there had been state terrorism, there wouldn't have been 900 victims from security forces, armed forces and civilians and 28...from supposed terrorists; the numbers would have been inverted."

Top officials in Gonzalez's old Socialist administration, including a former interior minister, are on trial for their alleged part in setting up, funding and running death squads against ETA activists in the 1980s.

ETA, which means Basque Homeland and Freedom in the Basque language, has killed about 800 people since starting a campaign for Basque independence in 1968 and was killing at a rate of about once a week when the dirty war was alleged to have started.

Ex-security chiefs and disgruntled Socialist leaders in the region have accused Gonzalez and his administration of organising the death squads, which murdered 27 alleged ETA members from 1983 to 1987.

Gonzalez said "incidents" such as these had happened in many other democratic states when confronting "terrorist activity". "Incidents like those that have occurred in Spain, have happened in every country where terrorist activity has struck out at democracy," he added.
